name: Shiki
description: TextMate-grammar highlighter using VS Code grammars and themes; hast IR, transformers, dual themes, JS or Oniguruma-WASM regex engine

host-language.comment: Written in TypeScript, ESM-only, consumed from any JS runtime (Node, Deno, Bun, browsers, workers).

form-factor.comment: Core library `shiki`; official CLI `@shikijs/cli` (commands `shiki` / `skat`) outputs ANSI or HTML.

license.comment: Code is MIT. Bundled grammars and themes (via tm-grammars/tm-themes) keep their upstream licences, described as permissive (MIT, Apache-2.0, etc.).

first-release.comment: Shiki's first npm publish was 0.0.2 on 2018-10-29, the same day the repo was created. The npm name also has a 0.0.1 from 2014, but that was an unrelated package (an ejs-like template engine by another author), so it is not counted.

engine-model.comment: Interprets TextMate grammars with a fork of vscode-textmate (@shikijs/vscode-textmate). The guideline says this applies whichever regex engine is chosen.

regex-engine.comment: Oniguruma compiled to WASM is the default. The alternative JavaScript RegExp engine transpiles Oniguruma patterns via oniguruma-to-es, and the docs say all built-in languages are supported as of 3.9.1.

embedded-languages.comment: The bundled HTML grammar (@shikijs/langs 4.6.0) imports the javascript and css grammars and uses TextMate injections/embeddedLangs, so HTML+JS+CSS works out of the box. Checked in the published package source.

language-auto-detection.comment: The language must be passed explicitly (`lang`). No content-based detection API exists in shiki 4.6.0.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: Languages are looked up by id or alias (e.g. `js`, `ts`), and some aliases match extensions. There is no built-in filename, extension, shebang or MIME lookup API; integrations map these themselves.

resumable-line-state.comment: `getLastGrammarState()` returns a GrammarState that can be passed back as `grammarState` to continue tokenizing from an intermediate state.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No edit-aware reparse. Only grammar-state resumption is available.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Uses TextMate regex state machines. Function-name scopes come from regex patterns, not from a syntax tree or locals analysis (per the guideline).

bundled-languages.comment: Counted 242 language ids in `bundledLanguagesInfo` (full bundle) in the shiki 4.6.0 package, excluding aliases. Some are variants (e.g. ahk/ahk2, html/html-derivative). The web bundle has about 57. Checked 2026-11-18.

grammar-format.comment: Grammars are TextMate grammar objects in JSON form, shipped as ESM modules.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Loads any VS Code / TextMate JSON grammar directly. tm-grammars normalizes grammars from their original upstream repositories.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: `highlighter.loadLanguage()` accepts a custom TextMate grammar object at runtime.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: All grammars, themes and WASM are served as ESM and lazy-loaded on demand as async chunks.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Rated 5 per the guideline (tracks mainstream upstream VS Code/TextMate grammars). tm-grammars is synced automatically from upstream repos, with daily publishing when there are changes. The JS engine in non-forgiving mode can differ slightly from Oniguruma. Based on sourcing, not on a systematic spot-check.

bundled-themes.comment: Counted 65 entries in `bundledThemesInfo` in shiki 4.6.0, checked 2026-11-18.

theme-format.comment: Uses VS Code JSON color themes. A css-variables theme can be built with `createCssVariablesTheme`.

token-classification.comment: Tokens carry TextMate scopes, and themes resolve them to colours. `includeExplanation` exposes the matched scopes per token.

css-class-output.comment: Inline styles by default. The official `transformerStyleToClass` (@shikijs/transformers) converts inline styles to generated CSS classes and emits the stylesheet.

multi-theme-output.comment: One `codeToHtml` call with `themes: { light, dark, ... }` stores each theme's colours as CSS variables (`--shiki-dark`, etc.). `defaultColor` options include `light-dark()`.

ir-kinds.comment: ThemedToken[][] has content, offset, color and fontStyle. Passing `includeExplanation` adds a scope stack per token. `codeToHast` returns a hast tree.

serializable-ir.comment: hast output qualifies per the guideline. Token arrays are also plain objects.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Tokens carry resolved `color`, `bgColor` and `fontStyle`. `codeToTokensWithThemes` returns per-theme variants.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: ThemedToken has an `offset` field (0-indexed start offset in the input), per the @shikijs/types 4.6.0 typings. Decorations also accept offsets or line/character positions.

custom-formatter-api.comment: Transformer hooks (preprocess/tokens/span/line/code/pre/root/postprocess) operate on hast. Custom renderers can consume `codeToTokens` or `codeToHast` output.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: Decorations API covers arbitrary ranges. Official transformers cover diff, highlight, focus, error level and word highlight notations.

output-formats.comment: HTML uses inline styles by default. Class output comes via the official transformerStyleToClass. ANSI comes from `codeToANSI` in @shikijs/cli, which uses ansis with a `colorLevel` option (1=16, 2=256, 3=truecolor; default 3). Hast is an IR, not a format. React/JSX rendering is documented through hast-util-to-jsx-runtime (third-party), so it is not counted.

line-numbers.comment: Provided by `transformerRenderLineNumber` in the official @shikijs/transformers. Otherwise, CSS counters are the usual approach.

streaming-output.comment: The official @shikijs/stream `CodeToTokenTransformStream` emits stable tokens line-by-line (optionally finer-grained with recalls) from a ReadableStream. It was previously antfu/shiki-stream (now archived and re-exporting it).

terminal-ready.comment: `codeToANSI` from @shikijs/cli. The CLI defaults to ANSI output.

native-dependencies.comment: The default Oniguruma engine ships as a WASM blob (onig.wasm, about 466 KB in shiki 4.6.0). The pure-JS RegExp engine avoids WASM entirely.

runs-in-browser.comment: Portable and does not use Node APIs or the filesystem. Can be loaded from a CDN (esm.sh) in the browser.

wasm-build.comment: Shiki itself is JavaScript and is not compiled to WASM. Only its optional default regex engine (Oniguruma) ships as WASM; see Native Dependencies.

synchronous-api.comment: `createHighlighter` is async, but highlighter methods are sync afterwards. `createHighlighterCoreSync` (since v1.16) is fully sync with the JS engine and pre-loaded langs/themes. The shorthands (`codeToHtml` from 'shiki') are async.

bindings-ports.comment: Phiki (PHP) is a separate reimplementation whose name and public API are inspired by Shiki. It is a port, not an official binding. No official bindings.

core-package-size.comment: @shikijs/core 4.6.0 is 35,982 bytes min+gzip (bundlephobia, 2026-11-18). That excludes the regex engine, grammars and themes. The `shiki` main entry is 65,418 bytes min+gzip before lazy chunks. Docs give 695 KB gzip for the web bundle and 1.2 MB for the full bundle including async chunks.

throughput-tier.comment: speed-highlight benchmark (Shiki 4.4 JS engine, Node 26, M4): 89,925 / 6,682 / 841 ops/min vs Prism 655,152 (tiny) and highlight.js 48,666 / 5,473 (medium/huge), about 6.5-7.3x slower than the fastest candidate in that benchmark. chsm.dev (Jan 2025, Oniguruma): about 7x slower than Prism. speed-highlight itself (not a candidate) is about 10-13x faster. Both benchmarks were run by a single author.

initialization-cost.comment: Cold start (import + first highlight) measured at 169 ms for Shiki 4.4 with the JS engine (speed-highlight benchmark). The docs say the highlighter instance 'is expensive to create'. Fine-grained bundles reduce this.

monthly-downloads.comment: npm downloads of `shiki` for October 2026 (calendar month). The rolling last-month figure (2026-10-18 to 2026-11-16) was 147,155,175. Checked 2026-11-18.

last-release.comment: shiki 4.6.0 was published to npm on 2026-11-02.

maintenance-status.comment: Frequent releases (latest 4.6.0 on 2026-11-02), last push on 2026-11-02, and the 4.x line is under active feature development. Checked 2026-11-18.

documentation-quality.comment: Dedicated docs site with guides, a language/theme catalog, package docs, migration guides (v0.14, Shikiji, v1 to v4) and blog release notes. API detail is spread across guides and the TypeScript typings.

notable-users.comment: Both verified from their official docs. Other widely reported users (e.g. Nuxt Content) were not verified this pass.

bus-factor.comment: Maintained under the volunteer `shikijs` GitHub org. Commits are dominated by antfu (about 1,036) and the original author octref/Pine Wu (about 960), followed by orta (about 159). There is no corporate backing.
